title: Two scheduled workflows turned main red every hour and every morning, for a billing reason no code change could fix, and reported it only in an annotation
detected_by: the session resolving CI, reading the annotation endpoint after `gh run view --log-failed` answered `log not found`

first_order.what_broke: ci-fleet-keeper (hourly, cron 17 * * * *) and ci-fleet-watch (daily, cron 30 6 * * *) both target `runs-on: ubuntu-latest`. This account cannot start a GitHub-hosted job at all, so both jobs conclude `failure` having run ZERO steps. main was therefore red once an hour and once every morning, on two checks that had nothing to do with any diff.
first_order.receipt: Run 32343624520, job 96347602802: {"conclusion":"failure","started_at":"2026-08-20T07:21:24Z","completed_at":"2026-08-20T07:21:27Z","steps":0}. `gh run view --log-failed` answers `log not found: 96371203101`. The only record anywhere is the check-run annotation, verbatim: "The job was not started because recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased. Please check the 'Billing & plans' section in your settings". Read it with `gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/check-runs/<job_id>/annotations`.
first_order.fixed_by: Both jobs moved to the fleet: `runs-on: ${{ vars.CI_LIGHT_RUNS_ON || vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'fly' }}` on ci-fleet-keeper's `keep`, `${{ vars.CI_RUNS_ON || 'fly' }}` on ci-fleet-watch's `watch`, and no `|| 'ubuntu-latest'` fallback in either, because on this account that fallback is not an escape hatch. Pinned by tests/unit/test_ci_fleet_keeper.py::test_the_keeper_runs_where_this_estate_actually_has_compute and tests/unit/test_ci_fleet_probe.py::test_the_watch_runs_where_this_estate_actually_has_compute.
first_order.first_fix_was_wrong: Between 09:00 and 12:30 on 2026-08-20 both jobs carried `if: vars.HOSTED_RUNNERS_AVAILABLE == 'yes'` instead, so they SKIPPED rather than failed, and the reply to the founder ended in 'fix Actions billing'. That stopped the red and stopped the checks with it: the variable was only ever going to be set after paying GitHub, and the founder's ruling is that we never will — "we are not paying for githuuub for the last tine, stop naking ne repeat". A check parked behind a switch nobody will flip is a check the estate has lost while still carrying its file, its tests and its name on the workflow list. Two tests now refuse that shape in both files: test_the_keeper_is_not_parked_behind_a_switch_nobody_will_flip and test_the_watch_is_not_parked_behind_a_switch_nobody_will_flip.

cause_chain: main went red on a schedule -> the failing job ran zero steps -> its log 404s, so the usual instrument returns nothing -> the reason lives only in a check-run annotation -> the reason is that account payments failed, which is a founder decision and not a code defect -> a check that is red every morning for a reason nobody in CI can act on is a check that trains the estate to ignore red.

second_order.premise_refuted: ci-fleet-keeper's own header argued that the Free plan's 2,000 GitHub-hosted minutes are an emergency reserve for ci.yml, whose runner label falls back to `|| 'ubuntu-latest'` when the CI_*_RUNS_ON variables are unset. That reserve does not exist. The fallback is an instant no-steps failure, which reads as nothing at all. If the fly pool ever goes down, ci.yml has no escape hatch.
second_order.why_running_on_the_fleet_is_safe: Both headers argued that a check on the fleet must not run on the fleet. That over-claimed. scripts/ci_fleet_keeper.py talks to https://api.machines.dev/v1 (line 67) and ci_fleet_probe.py shells out to `fly machine list` over FLY_API_TOKEN; neither inspects the box it runs on, so a runner started from a stale image still reports and repairs the fleet correctly. The one state genuinely lost is a TOTAL outage where no machine can pick the job up — answered by hand, as it always was: the ops console buttons, `scripts/ci_fleet_keeper.py --start` and `scripts/ci_fleet_probe.py --image-only`.

third_order.silence: The parked version added an `announce` job so the hourly skip would not be silent. With the jobs running for real there is nothing to announce, so it was deleted rather than kept as decoration.

grade.class: two classes, and the second is the expensive one. First: a failure whose only record is outside the instrument everyone uses — a job that never starts has no log, so `gh run view --log-failed` reports nothing and the run reads as unexplained. Second: ending a fix at an action only the founder can take. That is not a fix, it is a handoff, and it left two checks parked for ever behind a switch that was never going to be flipped.
grade.self_healing: not possible — the cause is a payment, which is the founder's alone
grade.guard: four tests across the two workflow files: two refuse a GitHub-hosted runner in any job, two refuse an `if:` gate on any job and refuse any mention of HOSTED_RUNNERS_AVAILABLE
grade.memory: we-are-not-paying-github-stop-asking.md — a workflow needing a hosted runner gets moved or deleted, never gated
grade.founder_action: none. Asking for one was the defect this record exists to close.
